guide.text: The sources are Harborlight's FY26 program report and the notes from a board retreat on September 13.
Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in fiscal year 2026, up from 936 the year before, and 71 earned a high school equivalency credential.
Operating expenses were $1,420,000, and 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, with an average wait of nine weeks.
Staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 that adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators.
Reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's 4-month target, and the board will vote on the budget on October 21.

questions.text: Reserves are at 3.2 months, short of the 4-month target. The FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 is $190,000 more than FY2026's $1,420,000. How will Harborlight cover that rise?
The waitlist holds 287 adults, and the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year. Why do staff expect it to cut the waitlist only in half?
Most of the 287 waitlisted adults are at the Eastgate and Riverside sites, but the sixth site is only at Eastgate. What happens to people waiting at Riverside?

brief.goal: Support the sixth site at the Eastgate branch library

lead.heading: More adults than ever want to learn, and 287 are still waiting

evidence.text: Harborlight enrolled 936 adult learners the year before FY2026.
In FY2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five sites, 212 more than the year before.
At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist, and the average wait was nine weeks.

points.heading: Learners who stay make real gains in reading and credentials

evidence.text: 68 percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more CASAS reading levels.
71 learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in Harborlight's history.
412 learners worked toward a high school equivalency credential, and 389 were English language learners.
A Riverside learner said: "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring."

points.heading: A sixth site at Eastgate meets demand where the wait is longest

evidence.text: Most of the 287 waiting adults were at the Eastgate and Riverside sites.
Today Harborlight runs five sites with four site coordinators.
The plan adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators.
Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year.
Staff estimate the sixth site would cut the waitlist in half.

points.heading: Volunteer tutors stretch every dollar spent on learners

evidence.text: 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours in FY2026.

counter.objection: Will our money really reach learners, or just add overhead to a stretched group?

evidence.text: Program costs were 81 percent of FY2026 spending.
Foundation grants provided $640,000 of FY2026 support.
Individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000.

P7.text: Present: board chair Lorraine Okafor, treasurer Dev Patel, executive director Marcus Bell, communications director Denise Alvarez, six board members.

P8.text:
The treasurer reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, below the board's target of 4 months.
The board asked staff to bring a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request to the October 21 board meeting.
Board members asked for a short deck they can use with funders when they talk about the sixth site.
The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

P1.text:
In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites, up from 936 the year before. Of those learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential and 389 were English language learners.
Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential, the most in the organization's history.

P2.text: A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. The average tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight employs 11 full-time staff, including four site coordinators.

P3.text:
Operating expenses for FY2026 were $1,420,000. Program costs were 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants provided $640,000, individual donors gave $388,000, and the city's adult education contract paid $295,000.
The cost per learner was $1,237.

P4.text: At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist, most of them at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks.

P5.text:
Staff recommend that the board approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library and two site coordinators. Staff estimate the sixth site would serve 180 more learners a year and cut the waitlist in half.
“I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring,” said a learner at the Riverside site.
